canonical_statement: A nondegenerate Borel probability law on the real line is stable if and only if it is the weak limit of positively scaled and centered convolution powers of some Borel probability law.
domain_and_universes: Borel measures on Real; natural convolution index; real positive scales and real centerings; proposition in Prop
hypotheses: nu is a Borel probability law
nu is not a Dirac point mass
conclusion: IsStableLaw nu if and only if there exists a Borel probability law mu and positive scales a_n with normalized convolution powers of mu converging weakly to nu

definitions.stability: For every n at least two, some positive affine normalization of the n-fold convolution of nu equals nu.
definitions.domain_of_attraction: There are positive scales and real centerings for which normalized convolution powers converge weakly against every bounded continuous real test function.
definitions.zeroth_convolution_power: dirac 0; asymptotic convergence makes this convention immaterial

excluded_degenerate_cases: ordinary Gaussian CLT as a substitute for the stable-law equivalence
foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory with mathlib classical measure theory, convolution, Bochner integration, topology, and bounded continuous functions; no custom axiom declarations
